title: Moments equal expectations under the uniform law
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity $n$, let $p$ be a natural number, and let $P$ be a probability measure on the Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$ that assigns to each singleton $\{x\}$ the uniform weight $2^{-n}$. Then the $p$-th moment of $f$ under $P$ equals the expectation of $f^p$ under the uniform measure:
\[
  \int f^p \, dP \;=\; \E\!\left[f^p\right] \;=\; 2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n} f(x)^p.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
P is a probability measure on the Boolean hypercube
P assigns each singleton the uniform weight 2^{-n}
replaced:
If $P$ is a probability measure on the cube assigning each point the uniform weight, then the
$p$-th moment of $f$ under $P$ coincides with the expectation $\E[f^p]$.
